messages:
sophie: Heads-up — UX pass for the Private setup step that runs connectivity checks. I pushed a quick prototype into Figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123 (see the panel called "Connectivity scan"). Looking for feedback on three things: progressive disclosure for advanced tests, the live narration for screen readers, and microcopy around IP ranges.

raj: Nice, thanks. Quick notes: the contrast on the green success chip is low against our bg, needs +4.5. Also, can we avoid the word "allowlist" in the UI? security team flagged it — suggest "Allowed IPs" or "Permitted IP ranges".

maria: Agree on the copy swap. Also the "Run full diagnostic" CTA feels scary. Maybe "Run extended checks" (less ominous). The quick/extended toggle should default to quick.

oliver: UX nit: when you hit "Run quick check" keyboard-only users lose focus — focus goes to the top of the page. We should move focus to the test results region (aria-live) so screen readers announce progress.

ux-research: From the lab: users don't understand why we ask for CIDR instead of single IPs. Proposed helper copy: "Enter single IPs or CIDR ranges (e.g., 203.0.113.5 or 203.0.113.0/24). We need this so Redwood can verify egress/ingress paths from your VPC." Also add a short "Why we ask for this" inline link that expands inline.

sophie: Good. For the helper we should show a one-line example of how to test from their host: ```bash
# run on your machine to confirm egress to our probe
curl -I https://probe-us.redwood.ai/ping
```

raj: Can we add an opt-in "scan-only" toggle that doesn't persist anything to the customer's account? Helpful for curious engineers. Label it "Local scan mode (no config saved)" with a tooltip.

maria: Accessibility: labels for the toggle and the detail disclosure must be programmatically associated. Also ensure the expanded explanation is reachable via keyboard (Enter/Space).

oliver: Layout idea: collapse advanced network tests (NAT traversal, port sweep, hostname v IP heuristics) into an accordion labeled "Advanced checks" and keep it collapsed by default. On collapse, show a one-line summary of last run status. That keeps the primary flow clean for new users.

ux-research: Lab finding: users skip reading long error messages. When a check fails, show a one-line actionable next step with an option to "See full diagnostic" for details. Example: "Port 443 blocked — ask infra to open outbound 443 to probe-us.redwood.ai or use the alternative TLS-port 8443".

infra-bot: Deploy note: probe-us currently accepts connections on 443 and 8443. If you want us to enable 9443 for isolated setups, file infra ticket #INF-789.

raj: Microcopy tweak: replace "Hostname" label with "Endpoint host (e.g., api.company.internal)" to reduce user confusion between instance name and DNS name.

sophie: Question for PMs — do we want to surface recent successful probe timestamps in the wizard? It could help troubleshooting but adds noise. Maybe a small "Last successful check: 2m ago" pill next to the Run button. Thoughts?

maria: I like the pill but make it visually subtle and keyboard focusable so screen reader users can read it. Use aria-label "Last successful check timestamp".

oliver: Also include a clear fallback path copy block for customers behind very restrictive egress policies: "If you cannot egress, open a support ticket and we can provide a one-time upload token to run an offline diagnostic." Link to KB.

ux-research: A11y regression: colour alone is used to indicate pass/fail in the timeline. Add icon + text and ensure errors have descriptive phrases (avoid just "failed"). Example: "Latency test: failed — TCP handshake timed out to 203.0.113.1:443".

sophie: I'll incorporate these. Final ask: copy suggestions for the scan summary card header — current: "Connectivity results". Alternatives: "Connection scan summary", "Network health check", "Connectivity report". Which is best?

raj: Vote: "Network health check". It's familiar to infra folks and less formal for product.

maria: Vote: "Connectivity report" — sounds friendlier.

oliver: Vote: "Connection scan summary" — concise and aligns with existing product wording.

ux-research: Leaning "Network health check" for lab clarity. But not a hill. Whatever we pick, make sure the H1 is consistent with the console's other pages.

sophie: OK we have split opinions — I'll do a quick A/B in the prototype and run a short hallway test. Last thing: design-bot, can you export a version with the aria-live region annotated and the collapsed state annotated for dev?

design-bot: Exported Figma frames: Connectivity-scan-aria + Connectivity-scan-collapsed. Link: https://figma.com/file/abc123?node-id=42. Added notes for dev: "aria-live=\"polite\" on #scan-results, focus after Run goes to #scan-results-heading".

infra-bot: FYI: we've added a non-production probe in eu-west for staging testing — endpoint: https://probe-eu.staging.redwood.ai/ping. Use only from staging.

maria: Awesome — thanks everyone. Sophie, ping when the prototype A/B is ready and I'll do a quick contrast + screen reader pass. :thumbsup:

sophie: Will do — thanks all :sparkles:
